newsitem.title: UK: EU states could fix EMU rules against UK - Heseltine.
newsitem.headline: EU states could fix EMU rules against UK - Heseltine.

text.p: Other European Union countries could fix the rules governing a single currency against Britain if the government prematurely ruled out joining monetary union, Deputy Prime Minister Michael Heseltine said on Friday.
"If you are not in the conference, have no illusions, those who are in the conference -- the Germans, the French, the Italians -- they will fix the rules against us," Heseltine told BBC television.
Eurosceptic members of the ruling Conservative Party have been urging the government to rule out ahead of the next election British participation in the single currency.
But the party's annual conference in the resort of Bournemouth has seen most elements of the party unite around Prime Minister John Major's wait-and-see stance.
Heseltine said the conference had seen a closing of Conservative ranks on the issue.
"People understood what was being said and they made up their minds that the Prime Minister and colleagues have got it right," he told his interviewer.
"They wanted you to know it, they wanted the Prime Minister to know it and they wanted the world to know it." REUTER
